item.title: MiBeeHive: The "Hive" Toolbox I Built for My Studio
item.description: Coming from an operations background, later transitioning to development, the number of projects I maintain keeps growing. Various middleware, databases, monitoring components… each version upgrade is a manual labor: go to the official site to find the download link, compare version numbers, manually download to the internal network, then distribute to each machine. I used to write a bunch of Shell scripts to periodically pull the latest versions to the LAN — functional but not user-friendly: scripts scattered everywhere, adding new software required writing parsing logic by hand, and there was nothing to check when things went wrong.

item.title: MiBeeBell: 30 Alerts In, One Notification Out
item.description:
One camera in my studio watches a hallway. Headlights sweeping past, a moth landing on the lens, tree shadows moving in the wind — all of it gets classified as motion detection. Dozens of alerts hit my phone in a night; once the push volume crosses a threshold I stop registering them, and the one alert that actually matters disappears into the noise.

For years the alerting here was improvised: the NVR pushed its own notifications, Steward’s device alerts went out as SMTP mail, and IoT device anomalies were dropped into an MQTT topic nobody watched. Channels scattered, no aggregation, no silence windows, and nowhere to manage the rules as a whole. MiBeeBell is the alert notification center I wrote for exactly this: every system sends its events to it, it does the noise reduction, and only the part worth interrupting you reaches a channel you picked. It is a CGO-free single binary in Go with SQLite for storage — Raspberry-Pi-class hardware can run it as a resident service. The name joins the MiBee studio brand with “Bell” — the bell a hive rings when something is wrong.

item.title: MiBeeReach: Remote Desktop, Terminal, SSH and Tunneling in One Binary
item.description: My complaints about commercial remote-access software are specific: the free tier throttles speed and caps hours, ads pop up on schedule, traffic flows through the vendor’s servers, and not one knob for image quality or latency belongs to me. I used Sunflower and ToDesk for a while and evaluated self-hosting RustDesk’s server edition before deciding to build one from zero. That is MiBeeReach: a single-binary remote access platform in Rust with remote desktop, remote terminal, remote SSH, tunneling, and cross-network P2P all inside. The name joins the MiBee brand with Reach — making any machine behind NAT reachable from outside, on your terms.

item.title: MiBeeVision: An Understanding Engine for MiBeeNvr's Recordings
item.description: The NVR keeps one promise: footage is always being recorded. Once the recordings pile up, a new problem appears — who watches dozens of gigabytes of playback? Scrubbing timelines afterwards to find “when did that person walk in” still relies on human eyes. MiBeeNvr’s browser-side AI watches the live view while the page is open, and stops the moment the tab closes. What is missing is a component that runs independently of any page, around the clock, over the recordings.
